we performed deep sequencing of a domestic animal virus to understand its replication strategy, and we identified two novel proteins that are likely to be important for virus replication.
the transcriptional landscape of torovirus is more complex than previously thought and that toroviruses encode two additional open reading frames that are conserved across the genus.

we used parallel sequencing technologies to analyze the relative levels of expression of the known toro- virus proteins and transcripts, and we also identified novel open reading frames and changes in host gene transcription and translation as an indirect result of torovirus infection.

the study of torovirus, which is a member of the Coronaviridae family of viruses that infects horses.
the molecular mechanisms of torovirus replication and how this relates to the evolution and biology of this group of viruses.
the transcriptional and translational landscape of equine toroviruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have provided an insight into the transcription and translation of the equine toroviruses and identified two novel proteins, U1 and U 2, that are encoded in the genome of this virus.
the authors have provided the first high-resolution transcriptional and translational analysis of a member of the Torovirus genus.

the results of this study have provided the first high resolution analysis of transcription and translational landscape of equine toroviruses, and have identified two previously unknown ORFs “hidden” within their genome, that are conserved and subject to purifying selective pressures across all toroviruses.

the transcriptional and translational landscape of equine toroviruses is now known.
we have identified a novel mechanism of torovirus sgRNA synthesis, and we have also identified two previously undescribed ORFs that are conserved in all available toroviruses.

we identified two new open reading frames (named U1 and U1) in equine toroviruses.
